title: LLM API GTM riposte and positioning notes
summary: Working draft: concise messaging and objection handling for conversations where prospects are already using or evaluating generic LLM API providers. Focus: move discussion from raw model access to predictable production inference (latency, cost, rollout, private deployment).
goals: Equip AE/SDR/SE with short rebuttals, demo hooks, and a feature checklist to highlight Redwood's production-first advantages vs commodity LLM APIs.
target_personas: Engineering leads (ML infra, platform), ML engineers (model ops), product managers for AI features, platform/security buyers for regulated data
one_liner: Redwood: the inference platform that makes LLMs predictable and economical in production — same API whether hosted, reserved, or private.
top_differentiators:
- Production-first SLAs and autoscale semantics (not just model access)
- Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private installs
- Cost controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization recommendations tied to real workloads
- Built-in graceful fallbacks (model variants, region/capacity routing)
- Strong observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and eval-linked regression alerts
competitor_signals: Common positioning we hear from vendors: 'we give the latest models fast' or 'lowest-latency endpoint' or 'simple pay-as-you-go pricing.' Typical blind spots: no dedicated capacity guarantees, limited private deployment options, opaque cost per request when you scale, weak rollout/rollback tooling.

sales_traps_and_rebuttals:
- They already use X provider because it's 'cheaper': cost slides are misleading at scale — ask about token mix and tail latencies; offer to run a 24h cost/latency sim using their top prompts.
- We can swap providers easily (vendor lock-in): switching is easy at small scale — ask about SLOs and fallbacks for peak traffic and audits; explain rollout policies and private deployment escape hatch.
- Latency is already fine: understand distribution (p50 vs p95/p99). If p99 spikes, show how dedicated pools + routing reduce long-tail. Share real customer p99 improvements.
- We prefer to self-host — want to control everything: validate ops burden: how many engineers to keep KB caches warm, tune kernels, handle GPU packing? Offer Redwood Private packaging and migration plan to reduce ops overhead.
- OpenAI/Anthropic are 'better models': models are one input; argue that serving, consistency, and cost at scale are often the gating factors for shipping features. Redwood supports curated model variants and validated perf/quality tradeoffs.
talk_tracks_by_persona:
- For ML infra: focus on autoscale semantics, KV cache behavior, kernel selection and quantization controls. Offer tech deep-dive + perf workbook.
- For product managers: emphasize predictable SLAs, stable unit economics, quality-monitoring alerts tied to prompt sets. Demo rollout + A/B.
- For security/compliance: highlight VPC/private, KMS integrations, audit logs and enterprise contracts. Bring up prior private deployments.
- For engineering manager (time-to-market): demo a migration template, and show how developer SDKs + consistent API reduce engineering work across hosted and private modes.
demo_script_snippet: 1) Start with the problem: show a p99 alarm and rising token spend over last 2 weeks. 2) Show Redwood Console: per-route token cost + p50/p95/p99. 3) Toggle a canary rollout from hosted->dedicated for a single route and show gradual traffic migration and fallback test. 4) Run a short workload: show batching and cache enabled vs disabled cost delta. 5) Show private deployment checklist and expected timelines.
metrics_and_proofs_to_use:
- Customer p99 latency drop (example: 320ms -> 90ms)
- Unit cost reduction from caching + batching (example: 18% token cost savings on chat workload)
- Successful private deployment case study: 6-week on-prem go-live
- SLA uptime percentage and incident MTTR average
pricing_objections_and_responses:
- 'Your price is higher per-token' => show unit-economics at scale and indirect costs (engineer ops, outages). Offer a trial with cost/latency snapshot.
- 'We need predictable cost' => propose reserved capacity pilot (3 month) with committed throughput and burstable buffer.
- 'We just want pay-as-you-go' => highlight mixed model: hosted for early usage, dedicated when predictable, private for regulated — same API across modes.
battle_rig_checklist_for_ae:
- Ask for top 20 prompts and current p50/p95/p99
- Request last 30 days token usage by route
- Check for private deployment constraints (VPC needed? On-prem?)
- Offer a 7–14 day perf+cost pilot
- Schedule SE deep-dive if p99 or SLOs are top concerns
